lessonSubtitle.organic: Preserving bone, wood, and natural materials
lessonSubtitle.textiles: Caring for ancient fabrics and fibers

section1.title: Why Ceramics Are Fragile
section1.content:
Ceramics have survived thousands of years underground in stable conditions. When unearthed, they face sudden environmental changes.

The main threats are mechanical shock (breaking), thermal stress (temperature changes causing cracks), and salt crystallization from moisture changes.

section2.title: Immediate Field Actions
section2.content:
Never clean ceramics in the field - dirt often holds fragments together.

Support the entire piece when lifting. Use both hands and keep it level. If cracked, do not attempt to separate pieces.

section3.title: Proper Storage
section3.content:
Use rigid plastic containers with custom-cut foam padding. The artifact should not move when the box is tilted.

Wrap in acid-free tissue paper. Store away from direct sunlight and temperature extremes.

section1.title: Understanding Metal Corrosion
section1.content:
Archaeological metals are chemically unstable. Exposure to oxygen and moisture triggers rapid corrosion.

Bronze disease, iron rust, and silver tarnish can destroy artifacts within hours of excavation if not properly handled.

section2.title: Controlling the Environment
section2.content:
Humidity is the enemy. Keep relative humidity below 40% using silica gel packets.

Never touch metals with bare hands - oils and salts from skin accelerate corrosion. Always use nitrile gloves.

section3.title: Safe Storage Methods
section3.content:
Seal metals in airtight containers with desiccants. Use chemically inert padding - never cotton or wool.

Monitor for color changes which indicate active corrosion. Document any changes immediately.

section1.title: Organic Material Sensitivity
section1.content:
Bone, wood, leather, and plant materials are extremely sensitive to environmental changes.

They can crack from drying too fast, or develop mold from excess moisture. Temperature swings cause expansion and contraction damage.

section2.title: Maintaining Moisture Balance
section2.content:
Keep organic materials at the moisture level they were found. If wet, keep them wet. If dry, keep them dry.

Wrap wet organics in damp (not wet) cotton or paper towels, then seal in plastic bags.

section3.title: Handling Guidelines
section3.content:
Minimize handling - every touch causes damage. Support fragile items on rigid boards.

Never attempt to unfold, unroll, or separate stuck materials. Leave all cleaning to professional conservators.

section1.title: Textile Vulnerabilities
section1.content:
Ancient textiles are among the most fragile artifacts. Fibers become brittle over time and can crumble at a touch.

Light causes fading and fiber breakdown. Even brief exposure to UV can cause irreversible damage.

section2.title: Light and Air Protection
section2.content:
Store textiles in complete darkness. Use opaque containers or wrap in acid-free tissue.

Avoid folding - roll textiles on acid-free tubes instead. Folds create permanent creases and weak points.

section3.title: Supporting Fragile Fabrics
section3.content:
Place textiles on flat, padded surfaces. Never hang or suspend ancient fabrics.

If a textile is stuck to soil or another surface, do not attempt separation. Transport the entire block to a lab.

section1.title: Critical Handling Rules
section1.content:
Scrolls and documents require the highest level of care. One wrong move can destroy thousands of years of history.

The golden rule: NEVER attempt to open, unroll, or unfold a scroll in the field. This is exclusively laboratory work.

section2.title: Environmental Stability
section2.content:
Maintain constant temperature and humidity. Fluctuations cause papyrus and parchment to expand and contract, leading to cracking.

Keep away from all light sources. Even indirect light accelerates degradation of inks and fibers.

section3.title: Transport Requirements
section3.content:
Support scrolls on rigid, flat surfaces that span their entire length. No part should hang unsupported.

Use sealed containers with climate control. Transport should be vibration-free - hand-carry when possible.
